title: OAuth Consent Phishing
narrativeSetup: You receive an email from 'Google Security' about a new app connected to your account.
messageContent: Please review the permissions granted to 'Google Drive Integration'. It requests access to 'Read, write, and delete all your Google Drive files'. Click 'Allow' to proceed to the review dashboard.
explanation: This is an OAuth consent phishing attack (Illicit Consent Grant). Instead of stealing your password, the attacker tricks you into granting their malicious app direct access to your data via Microsoft/Google APIs.

title: BGP Hijacking Alert
narrativeSetup: You are navigating to your bank's website. The connection is slow, and your browser throws a sudden SSL Certificate warning.
messageContent: Warning: Potential Security Risk Ahead. The certificate for www.chase.com is invalid. Error: SEC_ERROR_UNKNOWN_ISSUER. Proceed anyway?
explanation: Never bypass SSL warnings on financial sites. This could indicate a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack or a BGP route hijack where traffic is being rerouted to a malicious server holding a fake certificate.

title: Supply Chain Attack
narrativeSetup: You are a developer. You see a highly-rated npm package that solves your exact problem.
messageContent: Package: 'react-dom-utils'. Version 1.0.4 published 2 hours ago. 500 weekly downloads. Install via: npm i react-dom-utils
explanation: This is typosquatting (a form of supply chain attack). The real package is 'react-dom'. Malicious packages steal environment variables (like AWS keys) immediately upon installation via postinstall scripts.

messageContent: Phone call: 'Hi, this is Microsoft Windows Support. We've detected severe malware traffic originating from your IP address. Please press Windows+R and type eventvwr to see the errors.'
explanation: Microsoft does not proactively call users about malware. They are trying to trick you into opening the Event Viewer (which always shows harmless errors) to gain your trust and remote access.

title: MFA Fatigue Attack #2814
narrativeSetup: You receive an SMS alert that your Netflix account is suspended due to payment failure.
messageContent: You have received 15 consecutive login approval requests on your authenticator app. A follow-up SMS says: 'IT Support here, please approve the prompt to sync your mail.'
explanation: This is an MFA fatigue attack. The attacker has your password and is spamming you with requests hoping you'll accidentally approve one. Never approve unexpected prompts.
